newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks drop sharply in morning, property slides.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks drop sharply in morning, property slides.

text.p: A slide in property counters led Hong Kong stocks sharply lower in Thursday morning trade after the government made a move on Wednesday to cool down the local property market.
The Hang Seng Index was down 127.51 points, or 1.00 percent, at 12,648.88 after slumping to an early low of 12,597.71.
Turnover was HK$2.08 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.

The Hong Kong government said on Wednesday it would extend the presale period for private flats to 15 months from a current 12 months in a bid to increase supply and cool down escalating property prices.
"People are afraid that more serious tactics will be used by the government," said Peter Lai, an associate director at OCBC Securities.
Shares in Henderson Land Development Co Ltd fell HK$2.00 to HK$64.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd slumped HK$1.75 to HK$83.50.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd was down HK$1.25 at HK$69.25. The company posted a 23.7 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$13.77 billion on Wednesday, which was in line with market expectations.
Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities, said property stocks may remain under pressure in the short term but should find support soon following a lengthy correction.
Shares in Hutchison Whampoa Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$58.50. The Hong Kong conglomerate posted a 25.6 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$12.02 billion, also in line with expectations.
CITIC Pacific Ltd also reported results on Wednesday. Its net profit more than doubled in 1996 to HK$6.86 billion from HK$3.07 billion. The stock was down HK$0.40 at HK$38.10.

GITIC Enterprises Ltd moved lower on its second day of trading, falling HK$0.25 to HK$4.125, after an explosive market debut on Wednesday. The stock closed at HK$4.375 on Wednesday compared with an issue price of HK$1.05.
